title: Secure Cloud Operator Verification and Visibility

mission_brief.situation: As a cloud operator, I need to verify the identity of IAM users and ensure visibility into S3 bucket contents and EC2 instances.
mission_brief.mission: Verify user identity and list S3 bucket contents using AWS CLI.
mission_brief.execution: Describe EC2 instances to ensure accurate visibility.

prerequisites: AWS CLI installed on local machine

content.concept: Verification and visibility are essential for secure cloud operations. IAM users can be verified using AWS CLI commands, while S3 bucket contents and EC2 instances can be listed to ensure accurate visibility.
content.walkthrough: To verify user identity, use the `aws sts get-caller-identity` command. To list S3 bucket contents, use the `aws s3 ls` command. To describe EC2 instances, use the `aws ec2 describe-instances` command.
checkpoints: Verify IAM user identity using AWS CLI
List S3 bucket contents to ensure accurate visibility
Describe EC2 instances to confirm accurate visibility
common_mistakes: Incorrectly assuming IAM user identity without verification
Failing to list S3 bucket contents, leading to incomplete visibility
Ignoring EC2 instance descriptions, resulting in inaccurate visibility

lab.setup: Create an IAM user with necessary permissions and install AWS CLI on local machine.
safety: Avoid using AWS root account for operations
Regularly monitor IAM user permissions and revoke unnecessary access
Use AWS CLI commands to list S3 bucket contents and EC2 instances instead of manual checks

elite_competence.role_simulation: A cloud operator is responsible for verifying IAM user identity, listing S3 bucket contents, and describing EC2 instances to ensure accurate visibility.

bug_injection.bug: Incorrectly assuming IAM user identity without verification
bug_injection.symptom: Incomplete or inaccurate visibility into S3 bucket contents and EC2 instances
bug_injection.fix: Regularly verify IAM user identity using AWS CLI commands

pass_conditions: Verification of IAM user identity is accurate
S3 bucket contents are listed correctly
EC2 instance descriptions confirm accurate visibility
fail_conditions: Incomplete or inaccurate verification of IAM user identity
Failing to list S3 bucket contents, leading to incomplete visibility

interrogation_questions: What is the importance of verifying IAM user identity?
How can cloud operators ensure accurate visibility into S3 bucket contents and EC2 instances?
What are common mistakes that can lead to incomplete or inaccurate visibility?

legal_context.allowed: Using AWS CLI commands to verify IAM user identity, list S3 bucket contents, and describe EC2 instances.
legal_context.prohibited: Using AWS root account for operations, ignoring EC2 instance descriptions, and failing to regularly monitor IAM user permissions.

resume_bullets: Verified IAM user identity using AWS CLI
Listed S3 bucket contents to ensure accurate visibility
Described EC2 instances to confirm accurate visibility
